rounds.hypothesis: Both mugs should be released nearly centered over their respective plate origins, then drop 5 mm into stable plate contact while remaining well inside the strict 0.03 m origin-distance threshold. The porcelain mug is moved first to clear the central-left workspace before transporting the second mug toward the right plate.

The failed predicate was the white_yellow_mug_1-on-plate_2 goal because execution never passed that mug's grasp stage in three inits. The first mug and both placement heights are retained because every executed first placement succeeded and the complete run satisfied both predicates. The only substantive change is replacing the white/yellow mug's single low demonstration grasp with a collision-checked grid of higher, centered and oppositely shifted grasps, giving the guard alternatives after a post-close hand collision.

The first predicate and its entire motion were reliable. The failed predicate was white_yellow_mug_1 on plate_2 because execution usually stopped at that mug's post-close grasp guard, not because of transport or placement. The previous 30-candidate grid made matters worse because all candidates lacked the demonstrated handle-side longitudinal displacement and were rejected during approach. I therefore retained the successful order and all validated lift, transport, and placement values, replaced only the second grasp configuration, restored its demonstrated feasible orientation and height, and shifted the hand 10 mm farther outward from the mug body to avoid the observed palm collision while preserving handle reach.

The order and the entire porcelain-mug configuration are retained because that predicate succeeded in every run and moving it first clears workspace near the second mug. For the white/yellow mug, the evidence identifies the grasp as the primary failure: the 0.075 m hand height repeatedly contacted the mug, while the no-longitudinal higher grid was approach-infeasible. I therefore combine the demonstrated handle-side longitudinal geometry with the geometry-derived higher dz=0.0931 m, undo the unsupported extra 10 mm outward shift, and lower the release clearance from 5 mm to 1 mm to reduce post-release lateral motion. This should clear the mug body during grasp and leave the mug centered within the strict 0.03 m plate-origin radius.
